What We’re Looking For

The Climate Reality Project Canada is looking for our Community Climate Hub Manager who will provide leadership and guidance for the organization to support citizen-led climate action at the municipal level, anchored in a decentralised, collaborative and ambitious approach to solve the climate crisis through public policy literacy and accountability. This position will play a critical role in advancing climate education and action for our CRLs and Hub members across Canada. The selected candidate will work 28 hours per week, typically over four days but making allowances for flexibility required due to travel, work commitments, or other specific circumstances.

Who You Are

You are passionate about the mission of the Climate Reality Project to empower citizens from all paths of life and grassroots movements through a decentralised engagement model, and you are very familiar with climate science and policy. You enjoy strategic development and hands-on engagement. You are committed to solving the climate crisis through deep citizen engagement, organizing and multi-stakeholder convening. You are committed to diversity and inclusion, have a passion for social and environmental justice and an enthusiasm for operating in an intercultural work environment. You are a compassionate and natural convener, consensus-builder, meticulous problem-solver who loves to co-create, design and operationalize processes to support Hub members in building ambitious campaigns, help embed equity more effectively in our work, and use the team’s resources efficiently to maximize our real-world impact.

As well as being a strategic and systems thinker, the Community Climate Hub Manager will be someone who pays close attention to detail and deadlines and is exceptionally organized in their ability to assess priorities.

Position Description: The Community Climate Hubs Manager oversees the Community Climate Hub (CCH) program and related projects in order to nurture their success and to ensure they benefit each other while aligning with the organization’s strategic plan and overarching objectives. The DNA of this program is to build capacity and facilitate exchange among existing and new citizen-led Hubs, which are focused on coalition-building and public policy literacy to accelerate a just transition and raise ambition at the municipal level.

About the CCH program: Through the CCH program, grassroots campaigns are led by CRLs and citizens of all backgrounds to support rapid decarbonization of their municipalities. CCH drives sustainability at the municipal level by establishing citizen-led groups across the country and providing them with the tools and strategic support necessary to influence climate policy and to reduce their cities’ GHG emissions.

Two objectives steer the endeavor:

1. To move cities two steps forward along Federation of Canadian Municipalities (FCM) Partners for Climate Protection (PCP) 5-step Milestone Framework;

2. To obtain municipal commitments to net zero emissions by mid-century and then ensure the local governments are on track to reaching their target.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Manage the CCH program

o Coordinate, implement, monitor and manage the CCH project plans in terms of schedule, budget, achievement of goals and objectives to ensure alignment with the strategic objectives of the Climate Reality Project Canada.

o Develop, update, organize and expand the resources gathered in the CCH toolkit, keeping close attention to the best practices in distributed engagement and citizen participation in public policies.

o Develop, update, organize and expand the content of the CCH Handbook to ensure its relevance and complementarity to other citizen engagement tools. This task will require developing potential partnerships with peer organizations or grassroots movements.

o Manage the outreach campaign to recruit new Hub members and expand our CCH community.

o Drafting articles for the Climate Reality Project Canada to promote the CCH program and gain national visibility.

o Creation of presentation materials for the Hub members, supporting municipal policy solutions to solve the climate crisis.

o Represent the CRPC on municipal related questions.

o Support the Community Engagement Manager in engaging Climate Reality Leaders (CRLs) in local climate initiatives and in municipal climate consultations as well as policies.

o In partnership with the Community Engagement Manager, create opportunities of collaboration between Lead Mentors and Regional Organizers.

o Support the Regional Engagement Coordinator’s in the Maritimes, Rural Quebec, the Prairies and Northern Canada.

o Ensure the full provision of the CRPC communications associated with the programs overseen is available in French and English.

Manage the Regional Organizers

o Recruit and engage key Climate Leaders as Regional Organizers (ROs), and sustaining contact with them via email, telephone and conference calls, to ensure they have all the tools necessary to organize their communities and actively support the Hub captains and members.

o Provide support to ROs in the form of fact sheets and templates, to increase the number and quality of the acts of leadership delivered.

o Manage all of the administrative responsibilities associated with the ROs, including recruitment, hiring paperwork and payments.

o Coach the Hub Captains.

o Oversee the development the Hubs’ microsites and support the ROs with respect to associated technical questions.

Cities Caucus

o Represent CRPC on the Cities Caucus of the Climate Action Network Canada.

o Prepare and co-host the monthly calls.

o Rally participants around the tools and resources.

o Map the municipal citizen engagement across Canada to ensure that CRPC is at the forefront of grassroots-led movement at the municipal level.

Support the National Campaign Manager in their mandate and amplify all the CRPC’s National Campaigns amongst the CCH community and network.

Support the Communication & Social Medias Manager in reviewing any content related to the CCH program.

  • Assisting with special event organization, including but not limited to the National Climate League and the Climate Leadership Corps trainings.

Assist with the preparation of quarterly reports and any other required documentation.

Education & Experience:

  • Minimum 3 years’ experience in campaign coordination or a similar outreach, community engagement, network management or relationship building type role for an environmental or community organization.
  • Undergraduate degree in Environment, Political Science or related fields preferred.
  • Strong volunteers’ coordination and management experience required.
  • Having completed a Climate Leadership Corps Training is considered a strong asset.

Skills & Qualifications:

  • A passion for, and knowledge of, climate change science and solutions is required.
  • Fully bilingual in French and English; strong written and spoken skills in both languages.
  • Outstanding leadership and interpersonal skills.
  • Able to communicate professionally and effectively with people from all paths of life.
  • Excellent problem-solving ability.
  • Results-oriented mindset.
  • Very well-organized and detail-oriented.
  • Demonstrated experience with Microsoft Office, adept at Word processing, use of Excel spreadsheets, Airtable, data management, email software, web browsers.
  • Knowledge of Salesforce or similar CRM platforms is considered an asset.

To Apply:

Please send a resume and cover letter before 9:00PM on Thursday, April 29th, 2021 to André-Yanne Parent (she/her), Executive Director. Please note that only the candidates selected will be contacted.

The Climate Reality Project Canada is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, veteran status, marital status, sexual orientation, disability or any other category prohibited by local, provincial or federal law. This policy applies to all aspects of employment, including recruitment, placement, promotion, transfer, demotion, compensation, benefits, social and recreational activities and termination.

Who We Are
Founded and chaired by Nobel Laureate and former US Vice President Al Gore, The Climate Reality Project is dedicated to catalyzing a global solution to the climate crisis by making urgent action a necessity across every level of society. The organization has branches in 11 countries, including Canada, and over 31,000 volunteer Climate Reality Leaders. Over 1,400 of those Climate Reality Leaders (CRLs) are located in Canada.

The Canadian organization was established in Montreal in 2007 as a charitable organization, and has its own initiatives tailored to the Canadian context. We believe education is the key to the success of the climate movement. By spreading knowledge pertaining to climate science and by teaching citizens how to be effective communicators on the topic, we are empowering people to become impactful catalysts for change in their communities.

One of our key programs is the Community Climate Hub (CCH) initiative. Our organization builds on the fact that citizens have the power to not only amplify the ambitions of their local governments, but also to hold them accountable for their commitments by demanding concrete and measurable results. Since 2017, Hubs promote sustainability at the municipal level by creating and networking existing citizen-led groups across the country and providing them with the tools and strategic support needed to influence climate policy and reduce GHG emissions. With this initiative, our collective goal is toget local and municipal government to commit to net-zero emissions by mid-century. These commitments need to be rooted in justice and equity, and our organization will support their efforts to reach and exceed their objectives.

Are you an experienced climate and restoration leader ready to shape strategy and turn it into practical results? Do you enjoy developing services, building partnerships and bringing international teams together around shared goals? If so, this role could be the right fit for you.

What you can expect:

Preferred by Nature is looking for a Director of Climate and Restoration to lead our Climate and Restoration Programme within the Sustainability Certification division and coordinate climate and restoration work across our Advisory, Certification and Projects divisions.

Reporting to the Sustainability Certification Director, you will combine strategic and technical leadership with programme management, service development and external engagement. Our certification programme currently covers carbon project validation and verification, ecosystem restoration services, and verification of organisational and product carbon footprints. You will help this portfolio evolve in response to climate science, standards, regulation and market needs.

You will also lead our Climate Impact initiative, translating our ambition to build a strong portfolio of mitigation and adaptation services by 2028 into coordinated workplans and measurable progress.

Working with us is never routine, so in your first year you can expect the following areas to be central to your work.

  • Lead the Climate and Restoration Programme, ensuring effective service delivery and progress towards financial and impact targets.

  • Shape organisation-wide priorities for climate and restoration, aligning services, projects and expertise across divisions and regions.

  • Develop services and delivery approaches that respond to stakeholder needs and create meaningful environmental and social impact.

  • Oversee the systems, tools, templates and technical guidance needed for accreditation and credible service delivery.

  • Build strategic relationships with clients, companies, NGOs, governments, donors, producers and assurance schemes.

  • Identify and pursue business development, partnership and fundraising opportunities.

  • Represent Preferred by Nature in conferences, technical networks, industry initiatives and other external forums.

  • Lead and develop your team through clear priorities, capacity planning, regular feedback and professional development.

  • Contribute to strategic planning, programme budgets, financial monitoring and reporting.

Your first year with us:
Within three months, you will:

  • Develop a clear understanding of our climate and restoration portfolio, team capabilities, accreditation requirements and current commitments.

  • Build working relationships with colleagues across Certification, Advisory, Projects and regional teams, alongside key external stakeholders.

  • Review the Climate Impact roadmap and identify priorities, dependencies and opportunities for coordinated action.

Within six months, you will:

  • Translate agreed strategic priorities into workplans with clear responsibilities, resource needs and progress measures.

  • Work with relevant teams to advance priority service development, partnership and market engagement opportunities.

  • Establish regular programme reviews covering delivery quality, financial performance, impact and team capacity.

  • Put development priorities and training plans in place for your team.

Within twelve months, you will:

  • Demonstrate progress against the agreed Climate Impact workplan and programme objectives.

  • Have advanced priority services or partnerships that strengthen Preferred by Nature’s climate and restoration portfolio.

  • Strengthen coordination across divisions, with clear ownership and effective use of technical expertise.

  • Provide recommendations for the next planning cycle based on programme results, market developments and lessons learned.

Important that you:

  • Have at least 10 years of relevant professional experience, including substantial experience in senior leadership, programme development, stakeholder engagement and climate or restoration services.

  • Bring deep knowledge of climate mitigation, carbon markets, ecosystem restoration and related policy, market and regulatory developments.

  • Have a proven ability to set strategic direction and lead complex initiatives across multiple teams and stakeholder groups.

  • Can build alignment and deliver results in an international organisation where colleagues work across different functions and reporting lines.

  • Have experience developing strategic partnerships and identifying opportunities that support organisational impact and growth.

  • Bring professional credibility in the climate, carbon, restoration or wider sustainability sector, including experience representing an organisation in senior external forums.

  • Understand business development and fundraising, and have experience contributing to budgets and financial management.

  • Can lead and develop people, support teams through change and encourage collaboration, learning and accountability.

  • Combine an entrepreneurial approach with practical judgement and a focus on measurable results.

  • Share Preferred by Nature’s commitment to positive environmental and social impact.

Would also be great, but not necessary, if you:

  • Have worked across several areas of our current portfolio, such as carbon project validation and verification, ecosystem restoration, and organisational or product carbon footprints.

  • Have experience connecting assurance services, advisory work and project delivery within a shared organisational strategy.

If this sounds like you, we would love to hear from you!

What Sets Us Apart:

  • Global work culture

  • High degree of flexibility – remote work, work from home.

  • An in-depth onboarding and professional training that prepares you with the right skills and knowledge to thrive in this role.

  • Excellent opportunities for growth and professional development

  • Potential future international travel opportunities

  • A friendly, international team of colleagues, with a pleasant work environment

  • Start with 20 days of vacation leave per year

Preferred by Nature

Preferred by Nature is a non-profit, mission-driven organisation that works for sustainable land management and climate-friendly solutions. We develop practical solutions to drive positive impacts in production landscapes and supply chains, supporting better land management and business practices that benefit people, nature and the climate.

How to apply:

If you feel you meet the requirements of the role, please submit your application, including salary expectations, via the application form below. Application pre-screening will be conducted during the application period.

Preferred by Nature wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

AI Nexus NYC | C10 Labs
New York, NY | Flexible, Part-Time Mentor Engagement

About C10 Labs

C10 Labs is an AI-native venture fund and venture platform that partners with exceptional founders to build and scale category-defining AI companies.
Through AI Nexus NYC, C10 Labs brings together founders, investors, operators, researchers, corporate leaders, and industry experts to support the development and commercialization of high-potential AI startups.
We are expanding our mentor network and seeking experienced leaders across climate, sustainability, and environmental innovation who want to help founders solve meaningful industry challenges and build enduring companies.

The Opportunity

C10 Labs is seeking experienced founders, executives, investors, operators, researchers, and subject-matter experts to serve as Climate & Sustainability Mentors for AI Nexus NYC.
Mentors will work directly with early-stage founders developing AI-enabled solutions across climate technology, sustainability, decarbonization, resource efficiency, and environmental resilience.
This is an opportunity to provide practical guidance, challenge assumptions, make meaningful introductions, and help startups navigate complex markets, customer relationships, regulations, financing requirements, and commercialization pathways.
We are especially interested in mentors who can help founders move beyond product development and toward customer adoption, strategic partnerships, measurable impact, and institutional funding.

What You Will Do

Founder Mentorship and Company Building
  • Advise founders on product strategy, business models, market positioning, and commercialization.
  • Help startups identify their highest-value customer segments and use cases.
  • Provide practical feedback on go-to-market strategy, pricing, partnerships, and customer acquisition.
  • Challenge assumptions and help founders prioritize the opportunities that create the greatest commercial and environmental value.
  • Share lessons learned from building, operating, investing in, or scaling companies within climate and sustainability markets.
Customer and Market Development
  • Help founders understand how sustainability and climate-related purchasing decisions are made within large organizations.
  • Introduce startups to potential customers, pilot partners, corporate sustainability teams, investors, and industry experts when appropriate.
  • Advise founders on navigating long enterprise sales cycles and complex stakeholder environments.
  • Help companies design credible pilots and convert successful engagements into longer-term commercial relationships.
  • Provide insight into procurement, implementation, and adoption within regulated or operationally complex industries.
Climate and Sustainability Expertise
  • Help founders understand evolving industry trends, policies, regulations, reporting requirements, and market dynamics.
  • Provide feedback on environmental impact claims, sustainability metrics, and customer value propositions.
  • Support companies working through regulatory, technical, financial, or commercialization barriers.
  • Help founders distinguish between compelling climate impact and a scalable venture-backed business model.
  • Advise companies on how AI and data can create durable technical, operational, or commercial advantages.
Fundraising and Strategic Growth
  • Help founders refine their fundraising strategy and investor positioning.
  • Review pitch materials and provide feedback on how companies communicate their market opportunity, impact, traction, and differentiation.
  • Introduce founders to relevant climate investors, strategic partners, family offices, corporate venture groups, or grant and non-dilutive funding resources when appropriate.
  • Help startups understand the milestones required to become institutionally investable.
  • Support founders preparing for investor meetings, strategic partnership discussions, and diligence.
AI Nexus NYC Community
  • Participate in mentor office hours, workshops, panels, founder meetings, and community events.
  • Collaborate with other mentors, investors, operators, and C10 Labs team members.
  • Contribute insights that strengthen AI Nexus NYC programming and founder support.
  • Participate in Demo Day or investor-readiness activities when appropriate.

What We Are Looking For

We welcome mentors with experience across areas such as:
  • Climate Technology
  • Corporate Sustainability
  • Decarbonization
  • Carbon Accounting and Carbon Management
  • Carbon Markets
  • Climate Finance
  • Circular Economy
  • Waste Reduction and Resource Recovery
  • Sustainable Supply Chains
  • Environmental Data and Analytics
  • Climate Risk and Resilience
  • Water and Natural Resource Management
  • Sustainable Agriculture and Food Systems
  • Green Buildings and Infrastructure
  • Environmental Services
  • ESG and Sustainability Reporting
  • Clean Technology
  • Nature-Based Solutions
  • Climate Policy and Regulation
Who You Are
  • You enjoy helping founders work through difficult and ambiguous problems.
  • You bring practical operating, investing, technical, or market experience.
  • You are candid, thoughtful, and constructive in your feedback.
  • You understand that strong mentorship involves challenging founders, not simply encouraging them.
  • You are curious about how AI can create new solutions across climate and sustainability markets.
  • You want to help startups create measurable impact while building scalable and financially sustainable businesses.
Commitment

This is a flexible, part-time mentor engagement. Participation may include:
  • Founder mentoring sessions
  • Office hours
  • Workshops or panel discussions
  • Customer, partner, or investor introductions
  • Pitch and fundraising preparation
  • Demo Day participation
  • Periodic program and portfolio-company support
Mentor involvement will be coordinated based on availability, expertise, and the needs of participating companies.

Why C10 Labs

As a Climate & Sustainability Mentor, you will have the opportunity to work alongside ambitious founders developing AI-enabled solutions to important environmental and economic challenges.

You will become part of a growing community of investors, operators, researchers, corporate leaders, and entrepreneurs working to advance New York’s AI and innovation ecosystem while helping startups build stronger products, partnerships, and companies.

To Apply

Please submit your résumé or professional profile and a short description of the climate and sustainability areas in which you can provide the greatest value to founders.
C10 Labs welcomes mentors from diverse professional, academic, and industry backgrounds.

We are looking for a Climate Change Associate to implement and manage our rapidly growing portfolio of emission reduction projects globally. You will be responsible for the full project cycle of each project beginning from the initial due diligence to certification under international carbon and environmental attributes standards. The successful candidate will be based in India.

Responsibilities

  • Implement and manage emission reduction projects through the entire project validation, registration, verification, and issuance cycle
  • Draft technical project documents, feasibility studies, templates, concept notes, monitoring reports as per internal and external requirements in compliance with applicable standards such as VCS, Gold Standard, CDM, GCC, I-RECs and others as applicable
  • Conduct baseline and additionality assessment of projects including technical and financial analysis
  • Management of relationships with project owners, third-party auditors, standards, and other stakeholders
  • Work closely with the business development team in project due diligence, proposal preparation and provide expert advice
  • Conduct site visits to projects locations which may be remote and may require difficult travel conditions
  • Review technical documents prepared by team members and by third-parties such as auditors, project owners and partners
  • Follow internal guidelines, tools and software making sure key information and milestone remains up to date
  • Provide necessary training and guidance to team members on technical topics, project management, scheduling, and tools
  • Establish vision, strategy, goals, and priorities for Coral Future’s project portfolio and proactively seek new business opportunities
  • University degree in Engineering, Science, Economics or a related field or equivalent work experience (Master’s degree is a plus)
  • 2-5 years of Project Management or related experience is a plus. Fresh graduates are encouraged to apply
  • Excellent analytical, research, problem solving and decision-making skills
  • Ability to write high quality technical documents in English
  • Ability to explain complex topics in simple terms to various stakeholders
  • Skilled in managing timelines and targets and ability to handle multiple projects at the same time
  • Willingness to travel locally and internationally including to remote project locations
  • Outstanding communication and collaboration skills to partner effectively with key internal and external stakeholders
  • Comfortable operating in a fast-paced international multicultural environment
  • Ability to communicate effectively online using channels such as WhatsApp, Zoom, Google Meet, Skype and across multiple time zones
  • Skilled in using Microsoft Office and Google Workspaces
  • Professional fluency in both verbal and written English

Preferred:

  • Entrepreneurial mindset and big picture thinking
  • Decision-making ability based on cost-benefit trade-offs
  • Familiarity on issues linked to Climate Change, Renewable Energy and Sustainability is a plus

Please include a cover letter along with salary expectation describing how you might be a good fit for the position. Due to large number of applications, we will be able to contact only the shortlisted candidates.

We are quickly becoming a leader in offering innovative sustainability services to our clients globally. Our creative solutions have earned us brand recognition and a reputation for being a breath of fresh air in the industry. We believe that businesses need to be disruptive and creative in order to thrive and employees are our most important clients. If you are a smart, ambitious and dynamic sustainability professional who believes in making a real difference, this job might be for you.

At Our Children’s Trust, we are committed to providing an environment of mutual respect where equal employment opportunities are available to all applicants and teammates without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, physical and mental disability, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information, military and veteran status, and any other characteristic protected by applicable law. Our Children’s Trust believes that diversity and inclusion is critical to our success, and we seek to recruit, develop, and retain the most talented people.

Our Mission:

Our Children's Trust is a non-profit public interest law firm that provides strategic, campaign-based legal services to youth from diverse backgrounds to secure their legal rights to a safe climate. We work to protect the Earth's climate system for present and future generations by representing young people in global legal efforts to secure their binding and enforceable legal rights to a healthy atmosphere and stable climate based on the best available science. We support our youth clients and amplify their voices before the third branch of government in a highly strategic legal campaign that includes targeted media, education, and public engagement to support the youths' legal actions. Our legal work – guided by constitutional, public trust, human rights laws, and the laws of nature – aims to ensure systemic and science-based climate recovery planning and remedies at federal, state, and global levels. We seek legally-binding, countrywide and/or statewide science-based Climate Recovery Plans that will return atmospheric carbon dioxide concentrations to levels below 350 ppm by the year 2100.

Position Summary:

This is a voluntary, unpaid internship that will provide general support for OCT's strategic work in Washington, DC. There may be opportunities to work on Capitol Hill if you are located near or visiting DC.

Government affairs interns will directly support OCT's legal efforts in federal actions, including the constitutional and public trust climate cases filed against the federal government: Lighthiser v. Trump. and Venner v. EPA. Interns will have the opportunity to work on a variety of projects and potentially other cases. OCT relies heavily on interns for support, placing a premium on careful, accurate, and self-directed work. We are seeking experienced interns with excellent research, writing, and communication skills, and who are responsive, work independently, take initiative, are flexible and think creatively to find solutions. Previous political campaign experience is a plus.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Assist supervisor in advancing OCT's strategic legal campaign to compel government action to implement science-based climate recovery policies at all levels of the federal government.
  • Correspond and educate members of Congress and their staff on the disproportionate impacts of the climate crisis on the health, economic opportunity, and fundamental rights of children and the urgent demand for a climate recovery plan - a return atmospheric carbon dioxide concentrations to levels below 350 ppm by the year 2100 - to stabilize the planet. Secure cosponsors for the congressional resolution recognizing Children's Fundamental Rights to Life and a Stable Climate System. Track and perform legislative profiles and analysis on members of Congress. Join supervisor in virtual meetings with members of Congress, independently speak to staff members or act as team lead with youth groups. Coordinate virtual meetings with staff. Draft communications and advocacy materials. Perform outreach with organizations to garner endorsements to the resolution.
  • Manage and update multiple spreadsheets. Track climate and energy legislation and analyze the political landscape. Track legislative hearings, draft submissions of materials to the record, and take notes on relevant hearings. Identify opportunities for OCT to engage or share materials with members of Congress and staff.
  • Assist in garnering congressional and organizational support for amicus curiae briefs in support of the federal case.
  • Assist supervisor in identifying and making inroads with the administration in support of OCT's work. Perform research. Track, perform profiles and analysis on administrative officials. Identify opportunities for OCT to engage or share materials with the administration.
  • Build relationships and engage student and organizational partners in our campaigns through the Climate Rights Corps.
  • Track tasks to ensure accountability as assignments can require a short turnaround given the fast-paced nature of the work. Brief supervisor on the progress of tasks in daily to weekly conversations via Zoom, email, and phone. Attend and take notes at stakeholder meetings and weekly meetings with OCT attorneys and staff, if available.
  • Create a more diverse movement by identifying and networking with diverse allies in the legislative and executive branch and young leaders in BIPOC organizations and communities.
  • Opportunities for career development discussions will be provided.

Time Commitment:

ABOUT DSV

Deep Science Ventures (DSV) is on a mission to create a future in which both humans and the planet can thrive. We use our unique venture creation process to create, spin-out, and invest in science companies, combining available scientific knowledge and founder-type scientists into high-impact ventures. Operating in four sectors—Pharmaceuticals, Climate, Agriculture, and Computation—we tackle the challenges defining these areas by taking a first principles approach and partnering with leading institutions.

OUR PARTNERSHIP WITH RENAISSANCE PHILANTHROPY

Driven by mutual conviction in the huge unmet need for driving a new category of agricultural technology: priming resilience in crops,DSV has partnered with Renaissance Philanthropy to accelerate the development of venture creation at the intersection of climate risk, plant biology, and deployable agricultural products.

ABOUT THE ROLE

You will join DSV’s venture creation programme as a Founder-in-Residence and work closely with the DSV and Renaissance Philanthropy team to spin out the new company. During the programme you will refine, improve and complement existing scoping work on:

  • The technical thesis for crop systems that can be primed for resilience in the face of increasingly unpredictable and severe climate pressures (neglect and technical tractability);

THE OPPORTUNITY

Across global agriculture, climate volatility is no longer a ‘once-a-decade’ disruption - it is becoming an in-season operating condition. Drought and heatwaves are already driving severe regional harvest losses, with cascading impacts that reach far beyond the farm gate: price shocks, food insecurity, and destabilised livelihoods. Even where catastrophic crop failures are not occurring, the evidence base is clear that climate change is already depressing yields and amplifying climate-related production losses in major cropping systems.

Despite this reality, most crop resilience strategies remain anchored in a static view of risk. Today’s dominant approaches focus on breeding or engineering permanent stress tolerance into plants, or introducing permanent protective structures. While effective under chronic stress, these solutions come with an inherent trade-off: technologies that protect yield under adverse conditions present a burden when conditions are favourable. For many crops - particularly rain-fed cereals and broadacre systems - this ‘carrying cost’ is economically unacceptable. In practice, growers are left exposed to short, acute stress events (such as a brief heat spike during flowering or sudden water-logging after planting) that can irreversibly damage yield but do not justify permanent genetic or infrastructure compromises.

We believe this creates a compelling opportunity for a new paradigm: on-demand plant resilience. Instead of locking crops into a constant defensive state, plants could be temporarily primed to withstand stress only when risk is imminent - and then returned to a high-productivity mode once the threat passes. Advances across plant biology now make this vision increasingly plausible. Emerging tools such as RNA-based interventions, virus-enabled gene modulation, signalling peptides, and stress-responsive biologicals point toward the ability to transiently activate protective pathways, reprogram development, or stabilise yield-critical processes during vulnerable windows.

This approach has the potential to address not only extreme climate shocks, but also the everyday volatility that quietly erodes agricultural value: mistimed flowering, pre-harvest sprouting triggered by humidity, transient root-zone stress, or short droughts that reduce grain fill. Importantly, these interventions could be deployed in-season, aligned with weather forecasts or early stress signals, creating a more adaptive and responsive crop protection toolkit.

Commercially, this space remains wide open. Existing biostimulants and stress-mitigation products are often blunt, inconsistently effective, or poorly matched to specific climate risks. Meanwhile, large incumbents remain focused on conventional chemistry, genetics, or incremental biologicals, leaving little coordinated effort around truly inducible resilience platforms. At the same time, regulatory and technical signals show growing feasibility for novel biological and RNA-based crop inputs, while grower demand for tools that protect yield reliability under volatility continues to accelerate.

We are seeking a Founder in Residence to build a company at the intersection of climate risk, plant biology, and deployable agricultural products. The ambition is to create a platform that makes climate readiness a controllable, on-demand trait - integrating scientific insight, smart delivery, and clear grower ROI into a scalable venture capable of redefining how crops are protected in an unpredictable world.
